key_insight: DEEPRUBRIC improves reinforcement learning for deep research agents by building rubric supervision from evidence trees, so rewards better match what the task actually requires. This makes training more efficient and reduces the risk of rewarding superficial or misaligned answers.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the inefficiency of rubric-based RL for long-form research agents when rubrics are generated only from the query and fail to capture the full information need, evidence structure, and task scope.
method: Construct evidence trees that organize retrieved sources and supporting facts into a structured hierarchy.
Derive rubric criteria from the evidence tree rather than relying only on query-level rubric generation.
Use these evidence-grounded rubrics as checkable reward signals for reinforcement learning of deep research agents.
impact: This approach can make training research agents more reliable and sample-efficient, especially for complex open-ended tasks that depend on evidence coverage and reasoning quality. For practitioners, it offers a stronger path to aligning RL rewards with real report quality.

paper_title: DEEPRUBRIC: Evidence-Tree Rubric Supervision for Efficient Reinforcement Learning of Deep Research Agents
paper_authors: Minghang Zhu, Chuyang Wei, Junhao Xu, Yilin Cheng, Zhumin Chen
